q: The Federal Reserve System (the Fed) is the central banking system of which country?
explain: The Federal Reserve is the central banking system of the United States of America.

q: The World Bank provides loans to countries for capital projects. Where is it headquartered?
explain: The World Bank (and the IMF) are headquartered in Washington, D.C.

q: The European Investment Bank, set up in 1958 under the Treaty of Rome, is headquartered in:
explain: The European Investment Bank, the EU’s non-profit long-term lending institution, is based in Luxembourg.

q: The Bondi bond (Blockchain Offered New Debt Instrument) was issued by which institution, with Commonwealth Bank of Australia as organiser and main buyer?
explain: The Bondi bond was a blockchain-based bond issued by the World Bank, with Commonwealth Bank of Australia as organiser and main buyer.

q: Which country was the first borrower from the International Monetary Fund?
explain: France was the first country to borrow from the IMF, in 1947.

q: Which statement about the IMF is correct?
options: It can lend to any country in the world, member or not
It is not an agency related to the United Nations
It lends only to its member nations
It can lend directly to a State Government of a country
explain: The IMF lends only to its member nations. It is a UN-related institution and does not lend to state governments directly.

q: Voting rights in the IMF are distributed on the basis of:
options: Share of the country’s income in world income
Quotas allotted to countries from time to time
explain: IMF voting power follows each member’s quota, not one country one vote.

q: The headquarters of the IMF and the World Bank are located at:
explain: Both institutions are headquartered in Washington, D.C.

q: Which institution publishes the report called World Economic Outlook?
explain: The World Economic Outlook is published by the International Monetary Fund.

q: The capital (resources) of the IMF is mainly made up of contributions of the:
explain: Most IMF loan resources come from member countries, primarily through payment of quotas.

q: Which institution created Special Drawing Rights (SDRs)?
explain: SDRs were created by the IMF in 1969 as an international reserve asset.

q: Which World Bank Group institution is known as the soft loan window?
explain: IDA gives zero or very low interest loans on easy terms to the poorest countries, so it is the soft loan window.

q: The headquarters of the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) is in:
explain: IFAD is headquartered in Rome, Italy.

q: The headquarters of the World Trade Organization is in:
explain: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: The International Development Association, a lending agency, is administered by which institution?
options: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
explain: IDA is administered by the IBRD, the World Bank’s original lending arm.

q: Which member of the World Bank Group supports the private sector in developing countries?
options: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
explain: The International Finance Corporation (IFC) provides investment financing and advice to the private sector in developing countries. The IMF is not part of the group.

q: Which World Bank Group institution provides guarantees (political risk insurance) to promote foreign direct investment?
explain: MIGA, the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency, promotes FDI in developing countries through guarantees.

q: Arbitration of international investment disputes is the role of which World Bank Group member?
explain: The International Centre for Settlement of Investment Disputes (ICSID) provides arbitration on international investment disputes.

q: How many institutions make up the World Bank Group?
explain: The group has five institutions: IBRD, IDA, IFC, ICSID and MIGA.

q: Which World Bank Group institution provides debt financing to middle-income countries?
explain: The IBRD gives debt financing to middle-income and credit-worthy poor countries. IDA serves the poorest with interest-free loans.

q: The Bretton Woods Conference of 1944 was attended by delegates from how many nations?
explain: Delegates from 44 nations met at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, from 1 to 22 July 1944.

q: The two major accomplishments of the Bretton Woods Conference were the creation of:
explain: The conference created the International Monetary Fund and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development.

q: The IMF mandate was updated in 2012 to include:
options: All macroeconomic and financial sector issues bearing on global stability
explain: In 2012 the mandate was widened to cover all macroeconomic and financial sector issues that bear on global stability.

q: Which currency was added to the SDR basket in 2016?
explain: The Chinese Renminbi joined the US dollar, euro, yen and pound sterling in the SDR basket in 2016.

q: Which of these is NOT in the SDR basket of five currencies?
explain: The basket has the US dollar, yen, pound sterling, euro and Chinese Renminbi. The rupee is not included.

q: In which year did the IMF create SDRs?
explain: The SDR was created by the IMF in 1969 to supplement members’ official reserves.

q: IDA repayments are stretched over how many years, including a grace period of 5 to 10 years?
explain: IDA credits carry zero or very low interest, with repayment over 30 to 38 years including a 5 to 10 year grace period.

q: Debt relief through the HIPC Initiative and the MDRI is provided by:
explain: Besides concessional loans and grants, IDA gives debt relief through the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative and the Multilateral Debt Relief Initiative.

q: For how many of the world’s poorest countries is IDA a major source of assistance, as per the source?
explain: IDA is one of the largest sources of assistance for the world’s 76 poorest countries, according to the source.

q: On which date was the Asian Development Bank established?
explain: The ADB was established on 19 December 1966 to promote social and economic development in Asia.

q: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Development Bank?
explain: The ADB is headquartered in Mandaluyong, Metro Manila, in the Philippines.

q: The New Development Bank (NDB) was established by which group of countries?
explain: The NDB was set up by Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa (BRICS), with an agreement signed at the sixth BRICS Summit in Fortaleza, 2014.

q: In the NDB, the share of BRICS nations in voting power can never be less than:
explain: All UN members can join the NDB, but the BRICS share of voting power can never fall below 55%.

q: The New Development Bank is headquartered in:
explain: The NDB’s headquarters is in Shanghai, China. AIIB is in Beijing.

q: Where is the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) headquartered?
explain: The AIIB has its headquarters in Beijing, China.

q: AIIB began operations in which month and year, with 57 founding members?
explain: The AIIB began operations in January 2016 with 57 founding members; India has been a member since 2016.

q: Which country was expelled from the G-7 after the annexation of Crimea in 2014?
explain: Russia, a member since 1997, was expelled from the G-7 after it annexed Crimea in 2014.

q: The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) was founded in 1989 on the initiative of which group, to combat money laundering?
explain: FATF was founded in 1989 on the G-7’s initiative to develop policies against money laundering.

q: Where is the G-15 headquartered?
explain: The G-15 is an informal forum headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: The G-20 consists of 19 countries and which other member?
explain: As per the source, the G-20 has 19 countries plus the European Union. The African Union joined as a permanent member in 2023.

q: The E-9 forum was formed to achieve the goals of which initiative?
explain: The E-9 countries work for UNESCO’s Education For All; the E stands for Education and 9 for the nine countries.

q: Which of these countries is NOT a member of the E-9?
explain: E-9 members are Bangladesh, Brazil, China, Egypt, India, Indonesia, Mexico, Nigeria and Pakistan. Japan is not in the group.

q: The G-20 began in 1999 as a forum of:
explain: The G-20 was established in 1999 as a Finance Ministers’ forum; India has been a member since then.

q: Which of these is part of the G-7?
explain: The G-7 consists of the USA, Canada, Germany, Britain, France, Italy and Japan.

q: Which statement about the World Bank is correct?
options: It was founded under the Bretton Woods Agreement along with the IMF
It was founded in 1995 along with the WTO
It lends only to high-income countries
explain: The World Bank and IMF were founded together under the Bretton Woods Agreement, and the World Bank is based in Washington, D.C., lending to developing countries.
